title: Monster roster
prompt:
The starter reads a roster of up to eight monsters into `roster`, an array of structures. Each input line is a name of up to five letters, the monster's hit points, and its attitude, for example `Troll 88 -35`. Print the monster with the most hit points in this form:

```text
strongest: Troll, 88 hp, attitude -35
```

If two monsters tie, the one listed first wins. If the roster has no monsters, print `the roster is empty` instead.

A structure (a struct in C) is a group of fields stored side by side, each at a fixed distance, its offset, from the start of the structure. The starter names the offsets: the name at 0, the attitude at 6, the hit points at 8, and each monster takes 12 bytes, so monster i starts at `roster + i * 12`. Load each field with its own size. The attitude is a signed halfword (16 bits): a 32-bit load at its offset would also pick up two bytes of the hit points, and an unsigned load turns -35 into 65501.

## what is checked

- one line naming the strongest monster, or the empty-roster line
- the program exits cleanly
- the attitude is loaded as a signed halfword (`ldrsh` present)
- your program also runs on rosters you do not see: a tie, a single monster, an empty roster, the strongest listed last, and a roster where every monster has negative hit points
starter:
// read a roster of monsters into an array of structs and report the strongest
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(base_r, x19)
define(n_r, w20)
define(i_r, w21)
define(elem_r, x22)

define(MAX, 8)

// struct monster {
//         char  name[6];      // up to 5 letters and the zero byte
//         short attitude;     // -32768 (hostile) to 32767 (friendly)
//         int   hp;           // hit points
// };
name_o = 0                                  // field offsets inside one monster
attitude_o = 6
hp_o = 8
monster_size = 12

.data
fmt_n:      .string "%d"
fmt_in:     .string "%5s %d %d"
fmt_out:    .string "strongest: %s, %d hp, attitude %d\n"
msg_empty:  .string "the roster is empty\n"

.bss
.align 4
roster:     .skip 96                        // MAX monsters of monster_size bytes
count:      .skip 4
att_m:      .skip 4                         // the attitude as scanf reads it, a full int

.text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_n                  // how many monsters follow
        ldr     x1, =count
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =count
        ldr     n_r, [x9]

        cmp     n_r, 0                      // keep n between 0 and MAX
        b.ge    n_not_negative
        mov     n_r, 0
n_not_negative:
        cmp     n_r, MAX
        b.le    n_in_range
        mov     n_r, MAX
n_in_range:
        ldr     base_r, =roster

        mov     i_r, 0                      // one line per monster
        b       fill_test
fill_loop:
        sxtw    x9, i_r
        mov     x10, monster_size
        madd    elem_r, x9, x10, base_r     // elem = roster + i * monster_size
        ldr     x0, =fmt_in
        add     x1, elem_r, name_o
        add     x2, elem_r, hp_o
        ldr     x3, =att_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =att_m
        ldr     w10, [x9]
        strh    w10, [elem_r, attitude_o]   // the field keeps the low 16 bits
        add     i_r, i_r, 1
fill_test:
        cmp     i_r, n_r
        b.lt    fill_loop

        // TODO: when n is 0, print msg_empty. Otherwise find the monster
        // with the most hit points (a tie goes to the one listed first)
        // and print its name, hit points and attitude with fmt_out.
        // Load each field with the size it was declared with.

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
